citation.title: Topology optimization using artificial intelligence
citation.authors: Ahmed Ait Ouchaoui, Mohammed Nassraoui, Bouchaib Radi
citation.venue: Incertitudes et Fiabilité des Systèmes Multiphysiques, 8(2), 38–42
citation.version_coded: Version of record, open publisher PDF

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: On one cantilever case, TopologyGAN's reported stress, displacement, and deformation energy exceed SIMP's values by 2.72, 5.62, and 8.08 times, respectively.
claim.location: Section 3, Table 1 and results discussion, p. 41
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: The paper reports a 54-second computation but gives no comparable SIMP runtime, so a speed-up cannot be stated or derived.
claim.alternatives: The abstract and conclusion qualitatively claim improved computing performance/computational economy; no classical runtime comparison is supplied.

baseline.hardware_ml: ASUS computer, Intel Core i7-8565U CPU @ 1.80 GHz (reported with 54-second result; Section 3, p. 41)
baseline.problem_size: 120×60 mm domain, 1 mm elements, 7,200 elements (Section 2, p. 40)
baseline.ml_time: 54 seconds for the reported optimal shape; method attribution/comparability is unclear (Section 3, p. 41)
baseline.quality_metric: Maximum von Mises stress, maximum Y displacement, and deformation energy (Section 3, Table 1, p. 41)
baseline.quality_gap: TopologyGAN versus SIMP: stress 0.809 vs 0.297 MPa; displacement 51.097 vs 9.09 ×10⁻⁵ mm; deformation energy 41.79 vs 5.17 ×10⁻⁷ mJ (Table 1, p. 41).

R1.evidence: Section 3, Table 1, p. 41: the paper makes a qualitative computational-economy claim, while its GAN design has much higher reported stress, displacement, and deformation energy than SIMP; no matched-quality or matched-time comparison is shown.

R2.evidence: Sections 2–3, pp. 39–41: the classical solver implementation and hardware are not reported, so no R2 inefficiency criterion is established.

R3.evidence: Sections 2–4, pp. 39–42: a qualitative computational-economy claim is made without reporting training or data-generation cost.

R4.evidence: Section 3, Table 1, p. 41: the returned SIMP and TopologyGAN designs receive static structural evaluation and volume/weight reduction is discussed, but infeasible or failed-design rates are not reported.

notes: The paper describes a static cantilever comparison. It reports a 54-second computation but does not identify a comparable classical runtime; the qualitative speed/cost claim therefore cannot be quantified.
